subject: chem
title: Hydroxy Compounds
subtitle: Alcohols — classification, oxidation, dehydration and esterification.
concept: Alcohols are classified as primary, secondary or tertiary based on how many carbon groups are on the C–OH carbon.
Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes (distil) or carboxylic acids (reflux); secondary to ketones; tertiary are not oxidised by K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄.
Alcohols undergo dehydration to alkenes and esterification with carboxylic acids.

notes.heading: Classification and Oxidation
items: Primary (1°): one alkyl group on C–OH. Secondary (2°): two. Tertiary (3°): three — no H on C–OH.
Oxidising agent: K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄ (acidified dichromate). Orange → green (Cr⁶⁺→Cr³⁺).
1° + distil → aldehyde; 1° + reflux → carboxylic acid; 2° + reflux → ketone; 3° → no reaction.
Distinguish aldehyde from ketone: Tollens' reagent (silver mirror = aldehyde); Fehling's (brick-red ppt = aldehyde). Ketones give no reaction.

notes.heading: Reactions of Alcohols
items: Dehydration: conc. H₂SO₄ (or Al₂O₃, ~300°C) → alkene + H₂O.
Esterification: alcohol + carboxylic acid ⇌ ester + water; H₂SO₄ catalyst; reversible.
With Na metal: alcohol + Na → sodium alkoxide + H₂ (effervescence of H₂).
With PCl₅: alcohol + PCl₅ → chloroalkane + POCl₃ + HCl (white fumes of HCl).

definitions.body: Alcohol where the C bearing –OH is attached to one other carbon group.
Condensation reaction: alcohol + carboxylic acid → ester + H₂O (reversible, H₂SO₄ catalyst).
Ammoniacal silver nitrate solution — oxidises aldehydes to carboxylates, depositing a silver mirror; does not react with ketones.

workedExamples.q: How would you obtain pure ethanal from ethanol?

steps.text: Add ethanol dropwise to acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ (excess ethanol, hot).
Ethanal (bp 20°C) distils off as soon as it forms, preventing further oxidation.
Pure ethanal collected. Reflux would give ethanoic acid instead.

mistakes: Trying to oxidise tertiary alcohols — no H on C–OH, so no reaction.
Confusing aldehyde (positive Tollens'/Fehling's) with ketone (no reaction).
Forgetting esterification is reversible — use excess of one reagent to improve yield.
tips: Distil = stop at aldehyde; reflux = go to carboxylic acid.
Cr₂O₇²⁻ colour change is always orange → green — state both colours.
Ester name: ethyl ethanoate = ethanol (ethyl) + ethanoic acid.

flashcards.q: What colour change occurs when a primary alcohol is oxidised by K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄?
What is the product when propan-2-ol is oxidised?
flashcards.a: Propanone — a ketone (secondary alcohol oxidises to ketone).

flashcards.q: How do Tollens' and Fehling's tests distinguish aldehyde from ketone?
flashcards.a: Aldehydes: Tollens' → silver mirror; Fehling's → brick-red precipitate. Ketones: no reaction with either.

flashcards.q: What conditions cause dehydration of an alcohol?
flashcards.a: Concentrated H₂SO₄ (or H₃PO₄) and heat; or Al₂O₃ at ~300°C → alkene + H₂O.

flashcards.q: Write the equation for esterification of ethanol with ethanoic acid.
Why can tertiary alcohols not be oxidised?
flashcards.a: No H atom on the C bearing –OH, so oxidation cannot occur.

questions.q: Which product forms when butan-1-ol is refluxed with K₂Cr₂O₇/H₂SO₄?
questions.exp: Butan-1-ol is primary; reflux with Cr₂O₇²⁻/H₂SO₄ fully oxidises to butanoic acid.

questions.q: A compound gives a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent. What is it?
questions.exp: Aldehydes are oxidised by Tollens' reagent to produce a silver mirror — ketones do not react.

questions.q: What is the product of dehydrating ethanol?
questions.exp: Dehydration (elimination): CH₃CH₂OH → CH₂=CH₂ + H₂O (conc. H₂SO₄, heat).

questions.q: Which alcohol cannot be oxidised by acidified dichromate?
questions.exp: 2-methylpropan-2-ol is tertiary — no H on C–OH, so no oxidation.
Esterification is a condensation reaction — alcohol + carboxylic acid → ester + water.

recall: Classify primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols.
Describe the products of oxidation of 1° and 2° alcohols.
Explain how to distinguish aldehydes from ketones.
Write the equation for dehydration of propan-1-ol.
